data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 argues for the large centralized service but never engages the problem's core requirement: distinguishing failures that are truly independent from failures that merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found. Its mechanism (global observability and coordinated shedding) presupposes that the centralized entity can correctly identify correlated failure patterns in real time, but it provides no causal account of how to differentiate a genuinely independent scattered-failure pattern from a latent shared-cause failure that has not yet manifested fully. In fact, its own countercondition—a bad config push to all nodes—is exactly a shared cause that would be operationally invisible as 'correlated' until too late, yet the mechanism offers no evidentiary test to detect this. Without a causal mechanism for the distinguishing-evidence requirement, the argument fails the problem as stated.
